Apple's annual September event is about to take place, but according to all reports, one major product will be absent: the standard iPhone 18. Here's the expected launch timeline.

The standard iPhone 18 has been pushed back to early 2027 due to Apple's adjusted launch schedule.

The iPhone launch event is Apple's most important product announcement of the year. If the company fails to release its flagship new iPhone on schedule, investors are bound to be deeply concerned, which is one reason Apple has always maintained a steady iPhone launch cadence.

The event takes place in the first half of September each year (except 2020). Generally, the new iPhone lineup includes a standard model, two Pro models, and a fourth option, such as the iPhone Air.

But according to multiple reports circulating as early as May 2025, there will be no standard iPhone 18 next month.

This comes as quite a surprise, but so many sources have corroborated each other by now that it would actually be more surprising if the standard iPhone 18 did make an appearance.

Why is there no iPhone 18 at this year's September event?

We don't know the exact reason, but it may include the following:

  • Apple intends to space out its iPhone launches to accommodate more models, such as this year's iPhone Ultra.
  • Anticipated memory supply tightness, with Apple making adjustments to avoid severe shortages.

Regardless of the reason, the absence of the iPhone 18 from next month's event doesn't mean it's been cancelled. The standard iPhone 18 will still launch — just delayed until early 2027.

According to rumours, three models will be released next month: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra.

Then in early 2027, three more models will be unveiled: the iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, and iPhone Air 2.

The timing will likely be no later than March. Looking at past precedent, Apple launched the iPhone 16e in February and the iPhone 17e in March.

So if you want to get your hands on Apple's newest iPhone but don't want to pay the premium for a Pro or Ultra model, you'll need to wait a few more months.

What do you think of Apple's reportedly significant adjustments to its iPhone launch arrangements? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
